tools.name: get_public_report
tools.description: Retrieve an EXISTING public Evolize accessibility assessment for a website. Read-only: this starts no scan and creates no work. Returns not_found when no public report exists for the target — which says nothing about whether the site has accessibility problems. Evolize inspects publicly reachable pages of the target website in a real browser and runs deterministic accessibility checks (axe-core plus Evolize rules). It is not a local browser agent and it does not read your source code: findings reference the rendered DOM, so your coding agent maps them to source using its own repository access.

url.description: The public website to assess, e.g. `example.com` or `https://example.com`. Not an Evolize URL.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor`. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: scan_website
tools.description: Request an Evolize accessibility assessment of a publicly reachable website, then read the result with get_scan_result. By default a completed assessment up to 24 hours old is reused; pass refresh=true to require newly executed work (for example after deploying a fix). This CREATES work: it can start a real browser-based scan whose result is retained and may become a public report under Evolize's existing publication policy. Free public assessments are bounded: a completed result up to 24h old is reused unless refresh=true, at most 3 newly executed assessments per website per 24h, and the platform's own per-IP, per-domain and global scan limits still apply.

url.description: The public website to assess, e.g. `example.com` or `https://example.com`. Not an Evolize URL.

refresh.description: Require newly executed work instead of reusing a recent completed assessment. Use after deploying a fix. Never satisfied by an older completed report.

tools.name: get_scan_result
tools.description: Read the result of an Evolize assessment started with scan_website, using the scan_handle it returned. Read-only: it never starts a scan, never refreshes an assessment, never changes publication state, and never consumes scan quota — polling is safe. While the assessment is pending it returns the status and a retry_after_seconds. Follow next_cursor to read every finding.

scan_handle.description: The opaque handle returned by scan_website.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor`. Omit for the first page.
